## Purpose and scope

This notebook is the living reference for how **Collar (1990)** is used in this
project. Full citation: Collar, R.J., 1990, *Causes for the decline of hot spring
and geyser activity, Steamboat Springs, Nevada*: M.S. thesis, San Diego State
University (a by-product of the Collar and Huntley USGS grant study). It is **not**
the same document as Collar and Huntley (1990, 12th NZ Geothermal Workshop), cited
in `references.bib` as `collar1990`. Source files are in
`docs/literature/collar paper and plates/` (gitignored: cite, do not re-host). Plates 1-4
are unreferenced scanner TIFFs; they must be georeferenced in ArcGIS before any
coordinate is taken from them.

Every number below was read from page images of the thesis (Table 3 = thesis p. 152;
Table 4 = pp. 322-323), because the OCR text layer scrambles both tables.

```{r root-10}
#| include: false
if (basename(getwd()) == "notebooks") knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(file.path(getwd(), "..")))
```

```{r setup-10}
#| message: false
library(DBI); library(RSQLite); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2); library(knitr)
root <- "."
con <- dbConnect(SQLite(), file.path(root, "database", "geochem_operational.sqlite"))
source(file.path(root, "scripts", "analysis", "historical_comparison_collar1990.R"))
```

## 1. What the thesis contains and why it matters here

| Content (thesis pages, approx.) | Use in this project |
|---|---|
| Spring numbering and 1977-89 observations, main and low terrace (App. A, pp. 222-265) | Dated baseline of low-terrace features; White cataloged 20 low-terrace springs (9 geysers). By 1988 only spring 50 still flowed (about 3 gpm). |
| Fault and air-photo-lineament map, Plate 3 / Fig. 14 | Candidate source for digitized faults; shows Mud Volcano Basin, Steamboat Springs, Silica Pit, and Pleasant Valley faults and about 40 labeled wells and springs. |
| Chloride mass balance and Table 3 (pp. 150-154), App. D | Same method as the thesis; defines the creek reaches; supplies 1988-89 discharge. |
| Table 4 (pp. 322-323) | 86 station-date measurements of discharge, chloride, boron at 63 stations: transcribed to `data/raw/historical/collar1990_table4_stream_chemistry.csv`. |
| Barometric efficiency (pp. 56-64) | Spring 6: 42% (r = 0.79); spring 12: 45% (r = 0.44); White's low-terrace vent 31n: 60-75%. |
| Spa well, GS-1, spring 50 (pp. 81-85, 135-136, 154-155) | A pumped well near the low terrace produced weekday drawdown and weekend recovery in GS-1 and spring 50; main-terrace springs did not respond. |
| Earthquakes (pp. 52-56); precipitation (pp. 65-79) | Response thresholds and a cumulative-departure method for testing recharge. |
| Well logs (App. B, pp. 266-299) | 28 scanned NDWR driller's reports (strat wells 5-8, 13, 14, Cox I-1, Steamboat No. 1, the Spa well, and private wells), extracted and ingested (section 7). |

## 2. Collar versus Sorey and Colvard: one decline, two weightings

| | Collar (1990) | Sorey and Colvard (1992) |
|---|---|---|
| Principal cause of the 1986-89 decline | CPI field production, OESI to a lesser degree | Shallow South Truckee Meadows groundwater decline (80-95%) |
| Share attributed to production | "Principal" | 1-3 ft of about 17 ft (5-20%) |
| Agreement | CPI hydraulically connected to strat wells 2 and 9; terrace head fell about 17 ft; drought alone insufficient | same |

The disagreement is unresolved in the literature, and it is the right frame for any
2025 pressure or injection hypothesis.

## 3. Thermal discharge, 1955-2026, with the basis of each value

Only **creek-inflow** values are comparable with the SBRR-SBBV mass balance. White's 1955
total (1,125 gpm) includes 315 gpm from wells; creek-only is 325 + 485 = 810 gpm.

```{r discharge-table}
tbl <- build_collar_discharge_table(con)
kable(tbl[, c("source", "date", "basis", "gpm_low", "gpm_high", "Ls_low", "Ls_high")],
      col.names = c("Source", "Date", "Basis", "gpm low", "gpm high", "L/s low", "L/s high"))
```

Applying this project's two-station flux difference to Collar's own cleanest survey (same
date, March 4, 1989, S10 against S77):

```{r flux-check}
kable(build_collar_cl_flux_check())
```

The same-date two-station arithmetic gives about 32 L/s (508 gpm), against Collar's
reach-summed 660 gpm (42 L/s): about a quarter low. That bias is plausible for a survey
with distributaries and tributaries along the reach, and it applies to the 58.7 L/s and
27 L/s values as well.

## 4. Chloride at the two logger reaches

Station S10 is Steamboat Creek at Rhodes Road, immediately upstream of the Steamboat
Ditch inflow at S20 (Plate 4). Its chloride (17.2 and 23.8 mg/L) matches NDEP SB5
(median 14 mg/L, n = 143) and this project's SBRR (17.1 mg/L). The USGS gauge discharge
used for the SBRR flux (11.2 cfs, May 2026) is far larger than Collar's S10 flow (0.11 cfs
in August 1988, 2.5 cfs in March 1989), so whether the gauge sits above or below the
ditch inflow should be checked before that flux is treated as an upstream-control flux.

```{r cl-figure}
#| fig-height: 7
p <- build_collar_creek_chloride_figure(con, csv = file.path(root, "data/raw/historical/collar1990_table4_stream_chemistry.csv"))
print(p)
```

## 5. Candidate-cause checklist, Collar's tests applied to 2022-2026

```{r quakes}
sw <- read.csv(file.path(root, "data/derived/historical_comparison/swarm2024_waterlevel_step_check.csv"))
kable(sw, caption = "Standardized water-level step at STMGID wells around the four M3.0-3.5 events within about 6 km of the field (Jan-Mar 2024). Baseline SD is the SD of the same 3-day before/after statistic on all other days in Nov 2023-Jun 2024.")
```

Seven comparisons, standardized steps from -2.3 to +1.6: no consistent response, and the
single |z| > 2 is expected by chance in seven tests. The 2024 cluster stays a lead.

```{r weekday}
wk <- read.csv(file.path(root, "data/derived/historical_comparison/logger_weekday_periodicity_check.csv"))
kable(wk, caption = "Weekend-minus-weekday difference and Kruskal-Wallis test on daily mean temperature (15-day running mean removed), seven loggers.")
```

No weekday/weekend signal in temperature at any logger (all p > 0.7). Collar's spa-well
effect was in water level, so a pressure transducer in GS-1 or the resort-tank well is
the direct equivalent.

## 6. Plates: what to georeference and what is already known

`data/derived/historical_comparison/plate_georeferencing_features.csv` lists the Plate 3
and 4 features: 22 with coordinates already on file (use as control points), 24 to be
located from the plate (strat wells 2, 5-9, 13, 14, MacKay, Woods, Tangen, STMGID/Otten,
Towne, Byers, Gerold, the spa production well, and hot springs 50, 62, 63), and 5 to
digitize (four named faults and the ACEC box). Bianco's current database coordinate is
only a section centroid; Plate 3 shows it east of Highway 395 and can replace it.

```{r plate-table}
pl <- read.csv(file.path(root, "data/derived/historical_comparison/plate_georeferencing_features.csv"))
kable(pl[, c("plate_label", "plate", "category", "status")])
```

## 7. Appendix B well logs: lithology and log numbers

Thesis Appendix B reproduces 28 NDWR driller's reports (pp. 266-299). Each was extracted to its own PDF in `data/raw/ndwr/Collar_1990_AppB_well_logs/` (named by NDWR log number, 27 files; the Steamboat Spa log, 26097, was already staged from the NDWR download), read from the scans, and run through the existing well-log pipeline: OCR staging, human transcriptions (`well_log_manual_transcriptions.csv`, `well_log_lithology_manual.csv`), and promotion through `well_log_document_map.csv`. Log numbers were checked against NDWR's own table by owner, depth, and section; that check corrected or filled in nine log numbers where the handwriting or scan was unclear (for example Cox I-1 is log 22781, Strat 13 is log 28479, the Spa well is 26097, and Rogers is 20142, not 26142).

```{r appb}
d <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT d.log_number, COALESCE(w.well_name, '(staged, not linked)') AS well, d.depth_drilled_ft AS total_depth_ft, d.static_water_level_ft AS static_wl_ft, d.slot_from_ft AS perf_top, d.slot_to_ft AS perf_bottom, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Well_Lithology l WHERE l.source_document_id = d.document_id) AS n_lith FROM Well_Log_Documents d LEFT JOIN Wells w USING(well_id) WHERE d.source_batch LIKE 'Collar%' OR d.log_number = '26097' ORDER BY d.log_number")
kable(d)
```

Results: 13 wells are now linked to a confirmed log, including strat wells 5, 6, 7, 8, 13, and 14 (depth, construction, and 2-13 lithology intervals each, but still no coordinates), Cox I-1, Steinhardt, PTR-2, Herz Domestic, Peigh, and Bianco. Strat 2 and 9 are not in Appendix B. Three notes: (1) Bianco's log gives 110 ft, while Sorey and Colvard Table 3 lists 400 ft, so Table 3's Bianco may be a different well; (2) the Steamboat Spa production well (log 26097, 260 ft, 240 F, 30 gpm, 1985) is renamed from a provisional well and sits about 145 m from the SBW_0002 resort-tank sample, a strong but unconfirmed lead; (3) the Skalbeck-era meter depths for Herz Domestic and Peigh were converted to feet because the logs match them exactly. Wells still staged only (no confirmed Wells row): MacKay (2 logs), Woods, Tangen, STMGID (2), 1055 Lavender, Jeppson (2), Rogers, Boyd (1955, not the 1962 well), Curti (77 ft, not the 95-ft well on file), Steamboat No. 1 (21769, the original 21-5 hole, not the 21-5R redrill), and Towne (20106).
